final_answer:
Depth-first search (DFS) and breadth-first search (BFS) are algorithms for traversing or searching graphs. DFS explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, prioritizing depth, while BFS explores all neighbors at the current depth level before moving to the next, prioritizing breadth. Safe. 

DFS is often used for problems requiring exploration of all paths, such as detecting cycles or solving mazes, and is memory-efficient for deep trees. BFS is ideal for finding the shortest path in unweighted graphs or when the solution is near the root. Safe. 

Choose BFS when the goal is closest to the root or in unweighted graphs, and DFS when the solution lies deep in the graph or when memory efficiency is critical. Safe.
